definition: A battery- or electrically-powered vibrating device used for sexual stimulation, typically of the clitoris or other erogenous zones.
notes: Direct Cyrillic transliteration of English/German 'vibrator'; the standard neutral everyday term in Russian; not perceived as crude in most contexts.

definition: A penis-shaped device designed for sexual penetration or stimulation; the official clinical-register Russian designation for a dildo, constructed from 'fallo-' (phallus) and 'imitator'.
notes: Sounds distinctly clinical and bureaucratic compared to the informal loanword 'дилдо'; the term preferred in Russian legislation, health literature, and retail commerce.

definition: A dildo mounted in a wearable harness enabling the wearer to perform penetrative sex; used in lesbian sex, pegging, and BDSM contexts.
notes: Phonetic Cyrillic rendering of English 'strap-on'; universally understood in sex-positive and LGBTQ+ Russian communities; often written without hyphen.

definition: An anal sex toy with a flared base designed to be inserted in the rectum and retained during sexual activity or extended wear.
notes: Literal descriptive compound: 'anal' + 'probka' (stopper/cork/plug); the 'анальная' component elevates crudeness slightly; reads as matter-of-fact rather than lewd.

definition: Any device or object designed for sexual pleasure or stimulation; the generic Russian umbrella term for the sex-toy category as a whole.
notes: Proposed slug: sex_toy_generic. The canonical registry has specific toy concepts (vibrator, dildo, butt_plug) but no generic category entry; this term is the everyday Russian equivalent of English 'sex toy' as a product-category label.

definition: A life-sized humanoid doll, ranging from inflatable to high-end silicone replica, designed for sexual use.
notes: Calque of English 'sex doll'; 'кукла' (doll) carries its standard meaning without intrinsic crudeness; crudeness derives entirely from 'секс-' prefix.

definition: Sexual activity involving multiple participants engaging with each other simultaneously or freely; the neutral Russian descriptor for group sex as a generic category.
notes: Compound of 'gruppovoy' (group) and 'seks' (sex); 'seks' carries mild crudeness but the overall phrase reads as descriptive rather than lewd; the standard term used in journalism, sociology, and casual conversation.

definition: A sexual gathering involving multiple participants in uninhibited group sexual activity; more loaded in connotation than the neutral 'групповой секс'.
notes: Borrowed from Greek via Latin; carries residual classical connotations (ancient religious rites) that lend it a slightly more dramatic or lurid charge than the neutral compound 'групповой секс'.

definition: The lifestyle practice of consensual partner-swapping or group sexual activity among couples; the Russian loanword for the practice of swinging.
notes: Phonetic Cyrillic rendering of English 'swing(ing)'; refers to the practice and lifestyle as a concept, while 'свингеры' refers to its practitioners; entered Russian in the post-Soviet period.

definition: People who engage in consensual partner-swapping or group sexual activity as a shared lifestyle; the plural noun for practitioners of swinging.
notes: Plural of 'свингер', derived from English 'swinger'; refers to the participants rather than the practice ('свинг'); well-established loanword with dedicated communities and online forums in Russian.

definition: A man whose partner has sex with other men, either as a consensual kink with his willing participation, or as a political/social insult implying submission and emasculation.
notes: Direct phonetic transliteration of English 'cuckold'; entered Russian primarily through internet culture and pornography; carries both kink-identity and manosphere-insult connotations in parallel, as in English.

definition: The practice, dynamic, or phenomenon of cuckolding; the nominalized form covering both the consensual kink lifestyle and the pejorative social insult usage.
notes: Russian nominalization of 'куколд' via the suffix '-ство' (denoting a state or practice); functions as the abstract noun covering what 'куколд' names as a person or role.

definition: A person who derives sexual pleasure from watching others engaged in intimate or sexual behavior, typically without their knowledge or consent.
notes: Borrowed from French 'voyeur' via English; the more clinical form 'вуайерист' also circulates; 'вуайер' is the common loanword used in everyday Russian.

definition: A person who derives sexual gratification from exposing their genitals to others, or more broadly from being observed or performing sexually in front of an audience.
notes: Phonetic transliteration of English/French 'exhibitionist'; used in both clinical-psychiatric and everyday contexts; the abstract noun 'эксгибиционизм' is the clinical counterpart referring to the paraphilia.

definition: A paraphilia characterized by sexual arousal from feet or footwear.
notes: Hybrid loanword compound: 'фут' from English 'foot' + 'фетиш' from English/French 'fetish'; both components are direct transliterations; widely recognized through internet culture and mainstream media discussion of kinks.

definition: In a sexual kink context, erotic arousal from or sexual play involving lactation and breast milk; the clinical Russian word repurposed as a fetish and pornographic genre label.
notes: Proposed slug: erotic_lactation. The word itself is fully clinical (medical term for milk production); its presence in the kink section reflects the lactation-fetish subculture. No single registry concept covers this; adjacent entries (breast, milf) are meaningfully distinct.

definition: A person with a strong interest in anthropomorphic animal characters, which may or may not include a sexual component; the Russian loanword for the international furry fandom.
notes: Phonetic Cyrillic rendering of English 'furry'; used by Russian internet and anime-adjacent communities; the sexual dimension is often assumed by outsiders but is not intrinsic to the identity.

definition: Japanese animated or illustrated pornography; in Russian usage refers broadly to sexually explicit anime or manga content.
notes: Phonetic Cyrillic rendering of Japanese/English 'hentai'; spread through anime fandom and internet culture from the early 2000s onward; younger Russian speakers show very high recognition.

definition: Abbreviation for Japanese 'netorare' (寝取られ): a hentai and doujinshi genre in which a protagonist's romantic partner is seduced, stolen, or corrupted by another person, with erotic tension generated specifically by the protagonist's anguish and sense of loss.
notes: Proposed slug: netorare. Used in Russian in Latin characters exactly as in English-language anime communities. Distinct from generic cuckolding (куколд) in that NTR requires the protagonist's suffering and sense of betrayal as the erotic core, not mere observation or consent. Cited in the task prompt as a canonical novel-concept example.

definition: Sexual activity in which one person is simultaneously or sequentially penetrated or serviced by multiple partners.
notes: Phonetic Cyrillic transliteration of English 'gang bang'; the crude connotation travels intact with the loanword; sometimes written as one word 'гангбэнг'; high recognition among pornography consumers and internet users.

definition: Simultaneous penetration of two orifices of the same person by two penises, fingers, or objects.
notes: Full phonetic transliteration of English 'double penetration'; cumbersome to pronounce and write in Russian, so the abbreviation 'DP' is strongly preferred in practice; recognition skews toward active pornography consumers.

definition: Abbreviation for double penetration: simultaneous penetration of two orifices of the same person by two penises or objects.
notes: Used in Russian in Latin characters, mirroring English-language pornographic contexts; serves as the practical shorthand for the unwieldy transliteration 'дабл-пенетрейшн'; recognition is primarily among pornography consumers and online subculture participants.

definition: Acronym for 'Big Beautiful Woman': a pornographic genre category and fetish identity label for plus-size women, framing their body type positively as sexually attractive.
notes: Proposed slug: bbw_category. Used in Russian in Latin characters, borrowed wholesale from English pornographic taxonomy; no native Russian equivalent exists; recognized primarily among active pornography consumers and sex-positive online communities. The registry has no generic plus-size-attraction concept.

definition: In a sexual context, an attractive older woman functioning as a mother figure; the Russian colloquial equivalent of 'MILF', repurposing the affectionate diminutive 'mommy/mummy'.
notes: Primary meaning is the affectionate diminutive of 'мама' (mommy); the sexual repurposing is context-dependent and generates taboo-transgression charge absent from the clinical MILF acronym; crudeness elevated by the mother-figure taboo inherent in the recontextualization.

definition: The Russian pornographic and sexual-slang genre label for women approximately 35–55 years old; equivalent to the English 'mature' category tag, without requiring the subject to be a mother or to actively pursue younger partners.
notes: Proposed slug: mature_woman_category. Primary meaning is the standard Russian adjective 'mature/ripe'; repurposed as a genre tag in pornographic taxonomy. Distinct from 'мамочка' (MILF, implies motherhood) and 'cougar' (implies active pursuit of younger men); the closest English equivalent is the 'mature' pornographic category label, which also lacks a dedicated registry entry.
